title: Cycode: WinGet moderator triage tool could leak a GitHub token to a pull request's installer URL; Microsoft has fixed it
date_note: Cycode's post shows 'Last updated: November 18, 2026' and gives no publication or disclosure date; Expert Insights reported it on 19 November.
summary: Cycode reports that ManualValidationPipeline.ps1, a PowerShell triage tool used by moderators of the WinGet community repository, attached the moderator's GitHub Personal Access Token to every HTTP request it makes. Cycode says a pull request with an InstallerUrl pointing at an attacker's server could expose a Classic PAT with the workflow scope. Cycode says Microsoft has since patched it in pull request #456300; no in-the-wild exploitation is reported.
plain: Security firm Cycode says a tool used by Microsoft's WinGet moderators could have sent a powerful access token to an attacker through a single pull request. Cycode says Microsoft has fixed it.
exec: Cycode says the token could have been used to publish backdoored installers to WinGet's community repository; Cycode says Microsoft has patched it.
action: No action needed; for awareness. Cycode recommends moving from classic tokens to fine-grained tokens scoped to the microsoft/winget-pkgs repository.
impact: Cycode says the exposed token could have allowed publishing backdoored installers to 14,000 exposed packages; Cycode puts WinGet on over 1.4 billion active devices running Windows 10 and Windows 11. These are Cycode's figures.

validation.note: Cycode's own research post (Moriel Harush) read, plus Expert Insights (which quotes Microsoft's fix in PR #456300) and Ciberseguridad LATAM. Figures (14,000 packages, 1.4 billion devices) are Cycode's alone. Microsoft's own advisory was not read; no CVE was found.

review.note: Checked title, date, token type, PR 456300, fix and advice against Cycode, Expert Insights and Ciberseguridad LATAM; exec carried the 14,000 figure missing from the summary, so it was removed from exec (it stays in impact as Cycode's figure).
